newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-WEST INDIES WIN TOSS, PAKISTAN TO BAT.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-WEST INDIES WIN TOSS, PAKISTAN TO BAT.

text.p: West Indies captain Courtney Walsh won the toss and put Pakistan in to bat in a World Series limited overs match at the WACA ground on Friday.
Pakistan, who won a low-scoring match against Australia on Tuesday, dropped middle-order batsman Inzamam-ul-Haq.
Inzamam, one of the heroes of Pakistan's World Cup win in 1992, was replaced by Ijaz Ahmed Junior after a string of low scores.
Pakistan pace bowler Waqar Younis, who was expected to play after time off with a shoulder injury, remained out of the team after apparently failing a fitness test.
West Indies left out strike fast-bowler Curtly Ambrose, who is still nursing a hamstring injury.
The West Indies and Pakistan jointly lead the tri-nation series on six points each after five games, with host nation Australia languishing on four points from six games.
The winner of this match is virtually assured of a place in the best-of-three match series final later this month.
Australia are due to play West Indies in Perth on Sunday and must win to stay in contention for the finals.
West Indies - Sherwin Campbell, Junior Murray, Shivnarine Chanderpaul, Brian Lara, Carl Hooper, Jimmy Adams, Robert Samuels, Patterson Thompson, Ian Bishop, Adrian Griffith, Courtney Walsh (captain).
Pakistan - Aamir Sohail, Zahoor Elahi, Mohammad Wasim, Ijaz Ahmed, Mujahid Jamshed, Ijaz Ahmed Junior, Moin Khan, Wasim Akram (captain), Shahid Afridi, Saqlain Mushtaq, Mohammad Zahid.
